analysis.title: Power Back On? (GS Sector Specialists: Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview)
key_insights: Desk conversations over the last couple of days show investor concern on headwinds vs tailwinds for the power trade. Headwinds: midterms, rates, diesel, OEM overcapacity, lack of incremental data center contracts from behind-the-meter (BTM) players, PJM/ERCOT reforms, OH/TX/PA/NY headlines and NIMBY. Tailwinds: resilient hyperscaler capex, recent moves in PJM power price, bullish previews into year-end for BTM, general tightness in power over the next couple of years.

The prevailing playbook for the last couple of months was that power deal announcements would be more muted near term with polls and midterms in focus, but post-November and into year-end it could be off to the races.

IPPs: the main pushback for the last couple of months, that existing capacity might not obtain contracts with hyperscalers or data center customers, has been largely dismissed over the last 48 hours. GS sees signs of life for the group.

IPP investor mix: specialists are not tilted as negative and are starting to warm again. Generalist feedback has moved with headlines, but stacked contract wins have been directionally positive and some appetite remains. The trade has been PJM vs ERCOT for most, with debate over whether it is in middle or later innings into year-end.

BTM: specialist positioning is closer to 8/10 now and was likely closer to 10/10 in late summer. Optimism remains for more deal announcements into year-end, with positive updates over the last couple of weeks from AESI, PUMP and SEI.

BTM catalysts: focus on LBRT's path to a minimum of 500 MW into year-end, and a potential WMB BTM announcement at earnings or before year end. Financing and balance sheet capacity is topical and GS does not expect much to change there.
BTM dedicated investors are focused on Tier 1 vs Tier 2 operators and how customers sort names into those buckets.

Nuclear: the group has been under pressure for a couple of months. CEG's announcement on 6 Oct of 890 MW of uprates shows hyperscalers want reliable, clean baseload power. End users are happy to strike nuclear offtakes and PPAs, but construction and cost risk has kept more developers from announcing final investment decisions (FIDs).
Uranium read-through is positive, since uprates mean more demand.

sector_views.rationale: Pushback on the lack of hyperscaler contracts for existing capacity has eased over the last 48 hours. Specialists are warming and generalists still show some appetite.
Specialist positioning is about 8/10, down from about 10/10 in late summer. Deal announcements are expected into year-end.
Group has been under pressure, but CEG's 890 MW uprate announcement supports hyperscaler demand for clean baseload power, and uprates mean more uranium demand.

earnings_insights: WMB: a potential BTM announcement may come at its earnings or before year end (no EPS or revenue figures given).
risk_factors: Lack of incremental data center contracts from BTM players.
Financing and balance sheet capacity for BTM players.
Nuclear construction and cost risk delaying FIDs.
vol_and_positioning: Specialist positioning in BTM names is closer to 8/10, versus likely closer to 10/10 in late summer.
The IPP trade has mostly been PJM vs ERCOT, with debate over whether it is in middle or later innings into year-end.
Generalist IPP feedback has been headline-driven and described as rudderless for some time.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient hyperscaler capex, recent moves in PJM power price, bullish BTM previews into year-end and general power tightness. IPP contract pushback has eased over the last 48 hours.
tension_points.bear_case: Midterms, rates, diesel, OEM overcapacity, lack of incremental data center contracts from BTM players, PJM/ERCOT reforms, state headlines and NIMBY.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Post-November: the playbook expects deals to pick up after the midterms and into year-end, so continued absence of announcements would undercut it.
